page: Vultr voc-s-2c-16gb-320s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 2 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, translating to a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Powered by an AMD EPYC processor with an x86_64 architecture, the system operates with 1 physical core and 2 threads per core under a shared CPU allocation model. The hardware configuration includes 320 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and a single complimentary public IPv4 address, with no GPU acceleration.

Performance benchmarks reveal a mixed profile. The server achieves top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests and strong single-threaded compression and decompression capabilities. However, its shared CPU allocation introduces performance tradeoffs, as evidenced by weak multi-core PassMark scores, weak database operations, and poor static web serving throughput. Memory bandwidth remains average for large blocks but drops to the bottom 25% for small cached blocks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU density and substantial local NVMe storage without the premium of dedicated CPU cores. This makes it suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require continuous, sustained multi-core CPU utilization. Recommended workloads include lightweight caching layers, development environments, and memory-heavy background tasks with low parallel processing demands.
